Jess: Heads-up — HF->Redwood conversion on the new 7b-v2 candidate is producing weird token splits around our function-invoke markers; several evals fail with truncated JSON outputs.
Omar: Can you share a tiny reproducer (input + converted token ids)?
Jess: Minimal example: request contains a function tag like `<|fn:call|>{"name":"get_user"}` and after conversion/quant it becomes `<|f`, `n:`, `call|>`, `{` ... so our JSON-mode guard sees a broken opener.
Liang: That smells like tokenizer merges changing after quantization (vocab remapping). Are you using the conversion path that rewrites `config.json` special tokens?
Maya: Reminder: HF uses `add_special_tokens` entries while our importer expects a `special_tokens_map` and an explicit `token_ids` block. Missing the explicit ids lets the quant tool reassign them.
Jess: Repro steps I ran: 1) `git checkout model/7b-v2`, 2) `python convert_hf_to_rw.py --src . --out ./rw-7b-v2`, 3) quantize q4_0 via `rw-quant --model ./rw-7b-v2 --out ./rw-7b-v2-q`. Then run local eval harness `pytest tests/evals/tool-json --maxfail=1`. Logs show `json-mode: open brace missing` and `kvcache misalign` warnings.
InfraBot: Canary deploy started for rw-7b-v2-q at 1749990200 (canary=1).
Omar: Hypothesis: the conversion script writes special tokens as multi-codepoint strings and the quantizer's merges touch their byte piece splits resulting in different token ids. Two mitigations: pin token ids before quant or reserve an unused id range for special tokens.
Liang: Quick local experiment: patched convert_hf_to_rw.py to force-map special tokens to high unused ids before saving `tokenizer.json`. Patch snippet:

```
# inject special token ids to avoid merges
for name, tok in special_tokens.items():
    if tok not in tokenizer: tokenizer.add_special_token(tok)
    forced_id = tokenizer.vocab_size + reserved_offset
    tokenizer.set_token_id(tok, forced_id)
```

Omar: Nice. Did you run evals after that?
Liang: Yes — hellaswag subset: baseline 42.1 -> patched 49.8. Tool-call JSON unit tests: still flakey for nested arrays but much rarer.
Maya: We should also add an assert in the conversion pipeline: verify that every `role:` / `function:` marker serializes to exactly one token id. If not, fail the conversion and log example payloads.
Jess: Agreed. That would prevent silent regressions in production. Also saw one config quirk: HF chat templates with alias `</s>` sequences get stripped in our postprocess, which collapses adjacent markers — added a note in the PR.
Omar: I'll open a PR named `conv: preserve-special-token-ids + assertions` and include: (1) mapping to reserved ids, (2) conversion-time asserts, (3) regen script for existing models. Assigning @Liang for review and @Maya for tests.
Liang: LGTM, will add the bench job `bench/function-token-boundary` (1k examples) to catch low-rate regressions.
Maya: I'll add CI eval check that runs the bench after quantization so we catch performance/quality deltas early. Also adding a short post-quant token-diff tool to the repo.
Jess: I'll drop the failing eval logs and a tiny failing example in the PR description. Thanks — this should stop production surprises. :thumbsup:
Omar: One more note — we should document the mapping strategy in the onboarding checklist for new HF models (special_tokens -> reserved ids before quant). Saves future headaches.
InfraBot: Canary deploy completed at 1749990320 (status: rolled back due to unrelated OOM on canary host).
